## Purpose

This page verifies the exposure data of the study before any health analysis:
that temperature and air pollution cover the same municipalities and days, that
the heatwave indicators mean what the analysis plan says, and that the ozone
series are fit for use. It ends with the exposure dataset for 2009-2020 and the
points that need a decision.

The unit is the municipality-day: `r n_mun` municipalities (Santiago Province
plus Puente Alto) and the `r fmt(n_days)` days between 1 November and 31 March
of the calendar years 2009 to 2020, that is `r fmt(nrow(analysis))`
municipality-days.

## Inputs

| Input | Source | Content |
|---|---|---|
| CR2MET v2.5, municipal series | Center for Climate and Resilience Research, through the project's shared folder | Daily maximum and minimum temperature by municipality, 1980-2021 |
| Interpolated SINCA series, versions `opr` and `all` | Project team, `pollution-interpolation-kriging-idw` | Daily ozone, PM2.5, NO2, humidity and temperature by municipality, IDW and ordinary kriging, 1997-2026 |
| Hourly SINCA records | sinca.mma.gob.cl, 11 ozone stations of the Metropolitan Region | Hourly ozone, 2000-2026, with the validation status of each record |
| Station coordinates and target points | `pollution-interpolation-kriging-idw` | Location of the stations and of one point per municipality |

Every parameter used below is read from `config/config.yml`.

## Coverage of the three sources

Each source must hold exactly one row per municipality and day, for the same
days. The dataset keeps the three days before 1 January 2009 so that deaths of
the first days have their lagged exposures.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-alignment
#| tbl-cap: "Coverage of each source on the municipality-by-day grid."
alignment <- read_table("exposure_alignment.csv")
kable(alignment, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Source", "Rows", "Municipalities", "First day", "Last day", "Days",
                    "Repeated rows", "Missing from grid", "Outside grid"))
```

The three sources cover the same `r fmt(alignment$rows[1])` municipality-days
with no repeated and no missing rows.

## Calendars

### CR2MET has no 29 February

```{r}
#| label: leap-days
one <- read_cr2met(input_path("cr2met_tmax"), "tmax", study_municipalities()$code[1])
calendar <- seq(min(one$date), max(one$date), by = "day")
absent <- calendar[!calendar %in% one$date]
in_study <- absent[year(absent) >= 2009 & year(absent) <= 2020]
```

The CR2MET municipal files have `r fmt(nrow(one))` days between
`r format(min(one$date))` and `r format(max(one$date))`, against
`r fmt(length(calendar))` calendar days. The `r length(absent)` absent days are
all 29 February (`r paste(format(absent, "%Y"), collapse = ", ")`); three fall in
the study period (`r paste(format(in_study), collapse = ", ")`), which leaves
`r length(in_study) * n_mun` municipality-days without temperature.

The configuration sets `leap_day_handling` to
"`r get_param("temperature", "leap_day_handling")`": the pipeline fills those
days with the mean of 28 February and 1 March and marks them in `temp_filled`.
They are left out of the percentile calculations.

### Are the two calendars aligned?

A file with 365 days per year could also be shifted by one day after each
29 February. The check below correlates the day-to-day change of the CR2MET
maximum temperature with the day-to-day change of the SINCA station
temperature, moved between two days earlier and two days later. Aligned
calendars give the highest correlation at a shift of zero, in leap years as in
the others.

```{r}
#| label: fig-lags
#| fig-cap: "Correlation between day-to-day changes of CR2MET maximum temperature and SINCA station temperature, by shift of the SINCA series."
#| fig-height: 3.4
lags <- read_table("temporal_alignment_lags.csv")
ggplot(lags, aes(factor(shift_days), correlation)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, fill = colour_method[["IDW"]]) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", correlation), vjust = ifelse(correlation >= 0, -0.4, 1.3)),
            colour = ink$secondary, size = 3.2) +
  facet_wrap(~period) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.12, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = "Shift of the SINCA series (days)", y = "Correlation")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lags
#| tbl-cap: "Values behind the figure."
kable(dcast(lags, period ~ shift_days, value.var = "correlation"), digits = 3)
```

The correlation peaks at a shift of zero in both periods: CR2MET dates are
calendar dates and the only difference is the missing 29 February.

## Temperature thresholds

Percentiles of the daily maximum temperature of each municipality over
`r paste(get_param("temperature", "percentile_reference_years"), collapse = "-")`.
The reference code computes them over all days of the year
(`percentile_season: all_year`, the value in use); the table also gives the
thresholds that the warm-season days alone would produce.

```{r}
#| label: fig-thresholds
#| fig-cap: "95th percentile of daily maximum temperature by municipality, reference period 1990-2020, under the two season rules."
#| fig-height: 6.2
thresholds <- read_table("temperature_thresholds.csv")
thresholds[, rule := fifelse(season_rule == "all_year", "All days of the year", "Warm-season days")]
order_mun <- thresholds[season_rule == "all_year"][order(p95), municipality]
ggplot(thresholds, aes(p95, factor(municipality, levels = order_mun), colour = rule)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = get_param("temperature", "absolute_threshold_celsius"),
             colour = ink$axis, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("All days of the year" = "#2a78d6", "Warm-season days" = "#eb6834")) +
  labs(x = "95th percentile of maximum temperature (°C)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       caption = "Dashed line: the absolute threshold of 30 °C.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-thresholds
#| tbl-cap: "Thresholds of maximum temperature by municipality (°C)."
wide <- dcast(thresholds, com + municipality ~ season_rule, value.var = c("p90", "p95", "p99"))
kable(wide[order(com)], digits = 1,
      col.names = c("Code", "Municipality", "P90 all year", "P90 warm", "P95 all year",
                    "P95 warm", "P99 all year", "P99 warm"))
```

CR2MET municipal values are means over the whole area of the municipality.
Municipalities that reach into the Andes are therefore colder than their urban
area: the 95th percentile ranges from
`r sprintf("%.1f", min(thresholds[season_rule == "all_year", p95]))` °C
(`r thresholds[season_rule == "all_year"][which.min(p95), municipality]`) to
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(thresholds[season_rule == "all_year", p95]))` °C
(`r thresholds[season_rule == "all_year"][which.max(p95), municipality]`). A
fixed threshold of 30 °C means very different things across municipalities,
while the percentile thresholds adapt to each one.

## Heatwave indicators

A day is a heatwave day when it is at least the n-th consecutive day above the
threshold (n = 2, 3, 4), or when the excess heat factor of the last n days is
positive. The first n − 1 days of a hot spell are not flagged, as in the
reference code.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-heatwaves
#| tbl-cap: "Heatwave days in the warm seasons of 2009-2020 under the 15 definitions."
hw_columns <- grep("^hw_", names(analysis), value = TRUE)
hw_table <- rbindlist(lapply(hw_columns, function(v) {
  per_mun <- analysis[, .(days = sum(get(v))), by = com]
  data.table(indicator = v, municipality_days = sum(per_mun$days),
             share_pct = 100 * sum(per_mun$days) / nrow(analysis),
             per_municipality_year = mean(per_mun$days) / 12,
             min_municipality = min(per_mun$days), max_municipality = max(per_mun$days))
}))
kable(hw_table, digits = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Indicator", "Municipality-days", "% of days", "Days per municipality and year",
                    "Fewest in a municipality (12 years)", "Most in a municipality (12 years)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-heatwaves
#| fig-cap: "Heatwave days per municipality and year, by threshold and minimum duration."
#| fig-height: 3.6
hw_table[, threshold := factor(sub("^hw_(.*)_[0-9]d$", "\\1", indicator),
                               levels = c("p90", "p95", "p99", "30c", "ehf"),
                               labels = c("> P90", "> P95", "> P99", "> 30 °C", "EHF > 0"))]
hw_table[, duration := paste0(sub(".*_([0-9])d$", "\\1", indicator), " days")]
ggplot(hw_table, aes(duration, per_municipality_year)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, fill = ramp_orange[4]) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", per_municipality_year)), vjust = -0.4,
            colour = ink$secondary, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~threshold, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "Minimum duration", y = "Days per municipality and year")
```

### Consecutive days must be counted within each municipality

The reference script (`HeatWave_PretermBirth_Chile`, `Code/2.0 HW_process_data.R`)
builds the indicators with `lag()` on a table that holds all municipalities
stacked and sorted by date. As published, the previous row of a municipality is
therefore another municipality on the same day, not the same municipality on the
previous day. The chunk below applies that logic and the within-municipality
logic to the same temperatures and thresholds.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reference-lag
#| tbl-cap: "Heatwave days (> P95) in the 33 municipalities, warm seasons 2009-2020: lag over stacked rows against lag within municipality."
# All municipalities of the Metropolitan Region, in the column order of the file
raw <- fread(input_path("cr2met_tmax"), header = FALSE)
file_codes <- as.integer(unlist(raw[1, -(1:3)]))
rm_codes <- file_codes[file_codes >= 13000 & file_codes < 14000]
stacked <- read_cr2met(input_path("cr2met_tmax"), "tmax", rm_codes)
stacked[, file_order := match(com, rm_codes)]
p95 <- thresholds[season_rule == get_param("temperature", "percentile_season"), .(com, p95)]
stacked <- merge(stacked, p95, by = "com", all.x = TRUE)
stacked[, hot := as.integer(tmax > p95)]

# As published: rows sorted by date, municipalities stacked, lag over rows
setorder(stacked, date, file_order)
for (n in 2:4) {
  stacked[, (paste0("rows_", n, "d")) := as.integer(Reduce(`+`, shift(hot, 0:(n - 1))) >= n)]
}
# Within municipality, over consecutive calendar rows of the file
setorder(stacked, com, date)
for (n in 2:4) {
  stacked[, (paste0("within_", n, "d")) := as.integer(Reduce(`+`, shift(hot, 0:(n - 1))) >= n),
          by = com]
}
compare <- stacked[com %in% study_municipalities()$code & year(date) %in% 2009:2020 &
                     month(date) %in% get_param("study", "warm_season_months")]
for (v in grep("^(rows|within)_", names(compare), value = TRUE)) {
  set(compare, which(is.na(compare[[v]])), v, 0L)
}
lag_compare <- rbindlist(lapply(2:4, function(n) {
  a <- compare[[paste0("rows_", n, "d")]]
  b <- compare[[paste0("within_", n, "d")]]
  data.table(duration = paste(n, "days"), hot_days = sum(compare$hot),
             stacked_rows = sum(a), within_municipality = sum(b),
             flagged_only_by_stacked = sum(a == 1 & b == 0),
             flagged_only_within = sum(a == 0 & b == 1))
}))
kable(lag_compare, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Minimum duration", "Days above P95", "Lag over stacked rows",
                    "Lag within municipality", "Flagged only by stacked rows",
                    "Flagged only within municipality"))
```

With the stacked-row lag, a single hot day is flagged as a heatwave whenever the
neighbouring municipalities in the file are also hot that day, so the number of
heatwave days barely falls as the required duration grows. Counting within each
municipality gives the indicators used in this project. The published indicators
of the reference repository should be checked against this before they are
reused.

## Ozone and co-pollutants: delivered series

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pollution-qc
#| tbl-cap: "Quality rules applied to the delivered interpolated series, all days of the dataset."
pollution_qc <- read_table("air_pollution_qc.csv")
kable(pollution_qc, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Version", "Variable", "Method", "Rows", "Missing as delivered",
                    "Below zero, set to missing", "Fewer stations than the minimum, set to missing"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pollution-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Delivered series in the warm seasons of 2009-2020: distribution, stations and agreement between the two interpolation methods."
variables <- c(o3 = "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", pm25 = "PM2.5 (µg/m³)",
               no2 = "Nitrogen dioxide (ppb)", hum = "Relative humidity (%)")
pollution_summary <- rbindlist(lapply(names(variables), function(v) {
  idw <- analysis[[paste0(v, "_idw")]]
  ok <- analysis[[paste0(v, "_ok")]]
  st <- analysis[[paste0(v, "_n_stations")]]
  data.table(variable = variables[[v]], idw_mean = mean(idw, na.rm = TRUE),
             ok_mean = mean(ok, na.rm = TRUE), idw_missing = sum(is.na(idw)),
             ok_missing = sum(is.na(ok)), stations = sprintf("%d to %d", min(st), max(st)),
             correlation = cor(idw, ok, use = "complete.obs"),
             mean_abs_difference = mean(abs(idw - ok), na.rm = TRUE))
}))
kable(pollution_summary, digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Variable", "Mean, IDW", "Mean, kriging", "Missing, IDW", "Missing, kriging",
                    "Stations per day", "Correlation IDW-kriging", "Mean absolute difference"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-methods
#| fig-cap: "Ozone by ordinary kriging against ozone by IDW, delivered series, municipality-days of the warm seasons 2009-2020."
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-width: 5.2
ggplot(analysis[!is.na(o3_ok)], aes(o3_idw, o3_ok)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 70) +
  geom_abline(colour = ink$primary, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_magnitude(name = "Municipality-days", trans = "log10") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "IDW (ppb)", y = "Ordinary kriging (ppb)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.justification = "center")
```

### Version `opr` against version `all`

```{r}
#| label: tbl-versions
#| tbl-cap: "Ozone in the two delivered versions, warm seasons 2009-2020."
all_version <- fread(derived_path("exposure_air_pollution_all.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8",
                     select = c("com", "date", "o3_idw", "o3_ok", "o3_n_stations"))
all_version[, date := as.Date(date)]
versions <- merge(analysis[, .(com, date, o3_idw, o3_ok, o3_n_stations)], all_version,
                  by = c("com", "date"), suffixes = c("_opr", "_all"))
version_table <- rbindlist(lapply(c("idw", "ok"), function(m) {
  a <- versions[[paste0("o3_", m, "_opr")]]
  b <- versions[[paste0("o3_", m, "_all")]]
  data.table(method = m, municipality_days = sum(!is.na(a) & !is.na(b)),
             identical_pct = 100 * mean(abs(a - b) < 1e-6, na.rm = TRUE),
             correlation = cor(a, b, use = "complete.obs"),
             mean_difference = mean(b - a, na.rm = TRUE),
             p95_abs_difference = quantile(abs(b - a), 0.95, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
kable(version_table, digits = c(0, 0, 1, 3, 2, 2), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Method", "Municipality-days", "Identical (%)", "Correlation",
                    "Mean difference, all − opr (ppb)", "95th percentile of absolute difference (ppb)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-stations
#| tbl-cap: "Stations behind the ozone value, by version (share of municipality-days, %)."
station_counts <- rbind(
  versions[, .(version = "opr", stations = o3_n_stations_opr)],
  versions[, .(version = "all", stations = o3_n_stations_all)]
)[, .(n = .N), by = .(version, stations)]
station_counts[, share := 100 * n / sum(n), by = version]
kable(dcast(station_counts, stations ~ version, value.var = "share", fill = 0), digits = 1,
      col.names = c("Stations", "all", "opr"))
```

## Ozone rebuilt from the hourly records

Script 12 rebuilds the station series from the hourly SINCA records, with no
trimming and no imputation, as a 24-hour mean (`o3obs`) and as the daily maximum
8-hour mean (`o3mda8`), and interpolates them with the data author's model and
parameters. The reasons and the comparison with the delivered series are on the
[ozone validation page](03_ozone_validation.html).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-status
#| tbl-cap: "Hourly ozone records of the study period by validation status (% of hours)."
status <- read_table("ozone_station_hourly_status.csv")
status_cols <- setdiff(names(status), c("sinca_id", "station"))
status[, total := rowSums(.SD), .SDcols = status_cols]
status_pct <- status[, c(.(station = station, hours = total),
                         lapply(.SD, function(x) 100 * x / total)), .SDcols = status_cols]
kable(status_pct, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rebuilt-qc
#| tbl-cap: "Rebuilt municipal series: missing values and kriging diagnostics, all days of the dataset."
kable(read_table("ozone_rebuilt_qc.csv"), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Series", "Method", "Rows", "Missing", "Below zero, set to missing",
                    "Days with fewer than 3 stations", "Days with a variogram warning",
                    "Days without a fitted variogram"))
```

## Points to settle

```{r}
#| label: hot30
#| include: false
hot30 <- analysis[, .(share = 100 * mean(hot_30c)), by = municipality]
```

1. **29 February.** CR2MET has no leap days. They are filled by interpolation
   and flagged; the alternative is to leave them empty.
2. **Season of the percentiles.** All days of the year (reference code) or
   warm-season days only. The thresholds differ by about one degree.
3. **Heatwave indicators of the reference repository.** Its script counts
   consecutive days across stacked municipalities. This project counts them
   within each municipality.
4. **Fixed threshold of 30 °C.** With area-mean temperatures it is exceeded on
   `r fmt(max(hot30$share))`% of the warm-season days in
   `r hot30[which.max(share), municipality]` and on `r fmt(min(hot30$share))`% in
   `r hot30[which.min(share), municipality]`.
5. **Ozone metric and inputs.** The delivered series is a 24-hour mean built on
   trimmed and imputed station series; the plan names the MDA8. See the
   [ozone validation page](03_ozone_validation.html).
6. **Negative kriging values.** Set to missing and counted in the tables above.
7. **Three buffer days of December 2008.** The monitoring network of PM2.5 and
   NO2 was smaller before 2009; those days only feed the lags of the first
   deaths of January 2009.
